findings.evidence: DEFECT_REGISTRY.json's legacy DFF-031 entry claimed require_current_review_request_if_present 'blocked at pre-push' since PR #485, but that function has been an unconditional no-op since the exact commit that introduced it, with zero real test coverage (every reference stubbed it out) -- an overclaimed-prevention-state (DFF-015) instance discovered while investigating PR #535's live failure.

Live PR #535 evidence (exact HEAD c05da168545c5fa95fe300706eccaac2228fc391): after root causes 1 and 2 were fixed, hunter_merge_readiness_v2.resolve_review_authority misclassified a live, legitimate 'pending' (WAITING_FOR_REVIEWER, orchestration cycle genuinely published) verification result as a hard MALFORMED_REVIEW failure, so Hunter Merge Readiness could never reach the pending state its own sibling review_wait_state mechanism exists to produce -- an unrecoverable false failure, since no contributor push can complete a review a reviewer was never actually dispatched to perform.

Live PR #535 evidence (exact HEAD 0553514f411a9ef16053bce75678b5357c78d403): Hunter invoked Codex correctly via '@codex review', but treated the absence of a response after only ~300 seconds (codex's own ack_timeout_seconds/review_timeout_seconds, both capped at the pool's timeout_policy.max_seconds of 300) as sufficient to fail over through the reviewer pool, even though Codex's own normal hosted latency on this repository is ~20-30 minutes (PR #529 ~29min, PR #530 ~21min). Hunter failed over Codex -> Copilot -> Gemini -> Groq, where Gemini returned HTTP 503 and Groq HTTP 403.

Live PR #535 evidence (same exact HEAD): at least two Hunter Reviewer Collector runs (36340127965 and 36340195915) were dispatched for the same exact-head cycle, and the trusted orchestration status was republished with different reconcile trigger IDs for the same exact-head waiting cycle, despite ensure_collector persisting a cycle status before every dispatch -- because GitHub's combined-status read is not guaranteed read-your-write consistent, so a second, closely-spaced reconcile execution can still observe 'absent' after an earlier one already dispatched.

Live PR #535 evidence (exact HEAD 51108333821ab42d1ab7aa0b812a72d890f73795): the pull_request_target synchronize at 07:40:33Z triggered Hunter / Merge Readiness, Hunter / Trusted Preflight Upgrade and Hunter Governance Agent Preflight, but not Hunter Governance Review Reconcile and not Hunter Reviewer Collector for that exact HEAD. The only reconciliations that ran (36393517015, 36393716517) were workflow_run-triggered recoveries depending on other workflows' completions, and no trusted exact-head orchestration cycle was published for that HEAD, so Merge Readiness run 36393772215 correctly published MALFORMED_REVIEW: WAITING_FOR_REVIEWER. hunter-governance-reconcile.yml declared types: [ready_for_review] only, so Issue #534's earlier fix had covered one of the two transition classes that can invalidate the exact-head prerequisite and not the exact-HEAD-changing one. A secondary consequence of the same defect: because synchronize also fires on pushes to a Draft PR, once the trigger was added the trigger could no longer be the Draft guard, and the pre-existing structural regression had been asserting the defect itself ('synchronize' not in types).
